Feeling completely overwhelmed by my workload and schedule is the main source of my emotional distress, which makes me feel on edge and beat myself up. When it all gets to be too much, I just shut down, stay in my apartment scrolling on my phone, and avoid going to class or my maker meetup.\n\nDoctor: When you avoid activities like classes, work, or your maker meetup, is it because you feel like you're unable to cope with the demands of the situation, or is it more that you're trying to escape from the feelings of overwhelm and exhaustion?\n\nPatient: It’s really a combination of both. But I do also worry a lot about keeping up with my work and school, which leads to me beating myself up and zoning out on my phone instead of showing up.\n\nDoctor: Can you tell me if there's a specific aspect of your school, work, or social activities that you're avoiding due to fear of failure or evaluation, or is it more a general feeling of being overwhelmed that leads to avoidance?\n\nPatient: It’s definitely more of a general feeling of being completely overwhelmed by my new workload and schedule rather than a specific fear of failure. I just feel constantly on edge, and the sheer volume of work, school, and moving makes everything feel like \"too much.\" That's what causes me to shut down, avoid my classes and meetups, and just scroll on my phone instead.\n\nDoctor: Can you tell me if there's a point where you feel like you've completely given up on your goals and activities, or do you still hold onto the idea that you'll get back to them once you feel less overwhelmed?\n\nPatient: No, I haven't given up entirely. I still hold onto the hope that once I get used to this schedule and the workload settles into a solid routine, this overwhelmed, shut-down feeling will ease up. I really think I'll be able to handle things and get back to my normal activities once I adjust.\n\nDoctor: Can you describe if there's a specific difference in how you feel when you're avoiding activities due to feeling overwhelmed versus when you're engaging in avoidance as a way to escape from emotional distress, or do these feelings blend together for you?\n\nPatient: Honestly, those feelings pretty much blend together for me. Feeling completely overwhelmed by my workload and schedule is the main source of my emotional distress, which makes me feel on edge and beat myself up. That is ultimately what leads me to shut down, avoid everything, and just scroll on my phone.\n\nDoctor: Can you rate the intensity of your emotional distress when you're feeling overwhelmed, from 1 to 10, with 1 being mildly uncomfortable and 10 being extremely distressing?\n\nPatient: I'm not really sure of an exact number, and I haven't thought about it on a scale of 1 to 10. But it feels like a heavy, moderate level of distress that is actively disrupting my daily life and messing up my school and work.\n\nDoctor: Can you tell me if there's a specific aspect of your avoidance that is driven by a fear of negative evaluation by others, such as fear of being judged or criticized, or is it purely an internal feeling of being overwhelmed that leads to your avoidance?\n\nPatient: It is purely an internal feeling of being completely overwhelmed and unable to handle the pressure of my schedule, rather than any fear of being judged or criticized by others. While I definitely beat myself up internally for not coping well, the main driver is just feeling like everything is too much to face.\n\nDoctor: Can you describe if there are any times when you feel overwhelmed but are still able to push through and participate in activities, or does feeling overwhelmed always lead to avoidance and shutting down for you?"

Instead, I end up just sitting in my apartment scrolling on my phone and beating myself up for not handling things better.\n\nDoctor: Can you describe a recent situation where you felt overwhelmed and had to 'shut down' - was there a specific thought or worry that triggered your feeling of being overwhelmed, or did it feel more like a general sense of exhaustion?\n\nPatient: It’s really a mix of both, because I'm constantly on edge about falling behind while also feeling completely exhausted by this new routine. For example, the other day I was supposed to go to my favorite maker meetup, but instead I just stayed in my apartment scrolling on my phone, feeling totally shut down and beating myself up because everything felt like too much to handle.\n\nDoctor: Have you experienced a significant decrease in your overall productivity and efficiency, or is it more about feeling overwhelmed and avoiding activities due to emotional distress?\n\nPatient: It is definitely more about feeling completely overwhelmed and avoiding things due to the emotional distress. When the pressure builds up, I end up skipping my evening classes, swapping work shifts, and avoiding my maker meetup just to sit in my apartment scrolling on my phone. It all just feels like too much to handle.\n\nDoctor: Is your avoidance of activities like classes, work, and social events primarily because you feel exhausted and overwhelmed, or is it also because you're worried about not being able to perform well or make mistakes in those situations?\n\nPatient: It’s primarily because I feel completely overwhelmed and everything just feels like too much to handle, which makes me shut down and avoid going. But I do also worry a lot about keeping up with my work and school, which leads to me beating myself up and zoning out on my phone instead of showing up.\n\nDoctor: Can you tell me if there's a specific aspect of your school, work, or social activities that you're avoiding due to fear of failure or evaluation, or is it more a general feeling of being overwhelmed that leads to avoidance?\n\nPatient: It’s definitely more of a general feeling of being completely overwhelmed by my new workload and schedule rather than a specific fear of failure. When it all gets to be too much, I just shut down, stay in my apartment scrolling on my phone, and avoid going to class or my maker meetup.\n\nDoctor: When you avoid activities like classes, work, or your maker meetup, is it because you feel like you're unable to cope with the demands of the situation, or is it more that you're trying to escape from the feelings of overwhelm and exhaustion?\n\nPatient: It’s really a combination of both. I feel completely unable to handle the pressure and demands of this new schedule, which makes me feel so overwhelmed that I shut down and escape by sitting in my apartment scrolling on my phone to avoid facing how much I'm falling behind.\n\nDoctor: Can you tell me if there's a specific thought or situation that triggers your avoidance of activities, or is it more of a general feeling of being overwhelmed that leads you to shut down and avoid things?\n\nPatient: It is definitely a general, heavy feeling of being overwhelmed and falling behind rather than one single specific trigger. When I feel constantly on edge and feel like I can't keep up with both the factory job and the maintenance program, I just shut down, avoid going to class or my maker meetup, and sit in my apartment scrolling on my phone because it all feels like too much.\n\nDoctor: Can you describe how your avoidance of activities and shutting down has affected your daily life and relationships, and have you noticed any significant changes in your behavior or mood since you started feeling overwhelmed?\n\nPatient: It's completely disrupted my life because I've stopped doing things I love, like basketball, painting, and hiking, just to stay in my apartment scrolling on my phone. Even worse, I've missed several evening classes and had to swap work shifts last-minute, which led to warnings from both my advisor and supervisor. It's putting my spot in the tech program and my actual job at serious risk.\n\nDoctor: Can you tell me if there are any specific situations or tasks that you avoid due to feeling overwhelmed, but you're still able to force yourself to participate in or complete, or do you tend to avoid everything when you're feeling overwhelmed?\n\nPatient: When I get overwhelmed, I don't really force myself through things; I tend to just shut down and avoid almost everything. I end up skipping my evening classes, missing my favorite maker meetup, and even swapping my work shifts at the last minute just to stay in my apartment scrolling on my phone.\n\nDoctor: Do you feel like you're avoiding activities because you're worried about not being able to do them perfectly, or is it solely because you feel overwhelmed and exhausted by the thought of doing them?\n\nPatient: It’s definitely not about trying to be perfect. I just feel constantly on edge, and the sheer volume of work, school, and moving makes everything feel like \"too much.\" That's what causes me to shut down, avoid my classes and meetups, and just scroll on my phone instead.\n\nDoctor: Can you tell me if there's a point where you feel like you've completely given up on your goals and activities, or do you still hold onto the idea that you'll get back to them once you feel less overwhelmed?\n\nPatient: No, I haven't given up entirely. I still hold onto the hope that once I get used to this schedule and the workload settles into a solid routine, this overwhelmed, shut-down feeling will ease up. I really think I'll be able to handle things and get back to my normal activities once I adjust.\n\nDoctor: Can you describe if there's a specific difference in how you feel when you're avoiding activities due to feeling overwhelmed versus when you're engaging in avoidance as a way to escape from emotional distress, or do these feelings blend together for you?\n\nPatient: Honestly, those feelings pretty much blend together for me. Feeling completely overwhelmed by my workload and schedule is the main source of my emotional distress, which makes me feel on edge and beat myself up. That is ultimately what leads me to shut down, avoid everything, and just scroll on my phone.\n\nDoctor: Can you rate the intensity of your emotional distress when you're feeling overwhelmed, from 1 to 10, with 1 being mildly uncomfortable and 10 being extremely distressing?\n\nPatient: I'm not really sure of an exact number, and I haven't thought about it on a scale of 1 to 10. But it feels like a heavy, moderate level of distress that is actively disrupting my daily life and messing up my school and work.\n\nDoctor: Can you tell me if there's a specific aspect of your avoidance that is driven by a fear of negative evaluation by others, such as fear of being judged or criticized, or is it purely an internal feeling of being overwhelmed that leads to your avoidance?\n\nPatient: It is purely an internal feeling of being completely overwhelmed and unable to handle the pressure of my schedule, rather than any fear of being judged or criticized by others. While I definitely beat myself up internally for not coping well, the main driver is just feeling like everything is too much to face.\n\nDoctor: Can you describe if there are any times when you feel overwhelmed but are still able to push through and participate in activities, or does feeling overwhelmed always lead to avoidance and shutting down for you?\n\nPatient: Lately, feeling overwhelmed almost always leads to me shutting down and avoiding things instead of pushing through. I end up just staying in my apartment, scrolling on my phone, and skipping my classes, work shifts, or favorite maker meetups. It all just feels like way too much to handle, so I can't seem to force myself to participate.\n\nDoctor: Can you tell me if you've experienced any significant stressors or traumatic events recently, such as a major life change or loss, that might be contributing to your feelings of overwhelm and avoidance?\n\nPatient: Yes, I had a bunch of huge life changes hit me all at once about a month ago. I started my first full-time factory job, began a demanding industrial maintenance program at the community college, and moved out of my parents' house in Fayette into my own apartment. Trying to balance the shift work, rent, and heavy classes all of a sudden has just completely piled up on me and feels like too much.\n\nDoctor: Can you tell me if you've ever had a period in your life where you didn't feel overwhelmed and were able to manage your responsibilities and activities without shutting down, and if so, what was different about that time compared to now?\n\nPatient: Before all this, like back in high school, I managed my time fine and was busy but excited, still having plenty of time for hobbies like basketball, theater set design, hiking, and painting. But now, the sudden combination of living on my own, paying bills, working full-time shifts, and taking demanding evening classes has completely overwhelmed me and caused me to shut down.\n\nDoctor: Can you clarify if your avoidance of activities is primarily driven by a desire to escape from the emotional distress of feeling overwhelmed, or is it more about avoiding the tasks themselves due to feeling unable to cope with their demands?"
  }

I end up skipping my evening classes, missing my favorite maker meetup, and even swapping my work shifts at the last minute just to stay in my apartment scrolling on my phone.\n\nDoctor: Do you feel like you're avoiding activities because you're worried about not being able to do them perfectly, or is it solely because you feel overwhelmed and exhausted by the thought of doing them?\n\nPatient: It’s definitely not about trying to be perfect. I just feel constantly on edge, and the sheer volume of work, school, and moving makes everything feel like \"too much.\" That's what causes me to shut down, avoid my classes and meetups, and just scroll on my phone instead.\n\nDoctor: Can you tell me if there's a point where you feel like you've completely given up on your goals and activities, or do you still hold onto the idea that you'll get back to them once you feel less overwhelmed?\n\nPatient: No, I haven't given up entirely. I still hold onto the hope that once I get used to this schedule and the workload settles into a solid routine, this overwhelmed, shut-down feeling will ease up. I really think I'll be able to handle things and get back to my normal activities once I adjust.\n\nDoctor: Can you describe if there's a specific difference in how you feel when you're avoiding activities due to feeling overwhelmed versus when you're engaging in avoidance as a way to escape from emotional distress, or do these feelings blend together for you?\n\nPatient: Honestly, those feelings pretty much blend together for me. Feeling completely overwhelmed by my workload and schedule is the main source of my emotional distress, which makes me feel on edge and beat myself up. That is ultimately what leads me to shut down, avoid everything, and just scroll on my phone.\n\nDoctor: Can you rate the intensity of your emotional distress when you're feeling overwhelmed, from 1 to 10, with 1 being mildly uncomfortable and 10 being extremely distressing?\n\nPatient: I'm not really sure of an exact number, and I haven't thought about it on a scale of 1 to 10. But it feels like a heavy, moderate level of distress that is actively disrupting my daily life and messing up my school and work.\n\nDoctor: Can you tell me if there's a specific aspect of your avoidance that is driven by a fear of negative evaluation by others, such as fear of being judged or criticized, or is it purely an internal feeling of being overwhelmed that leads to your avoidance?\n\nPatient: It is purely an internal feeling of being completely overwhelmed and unable to handle the pressure of my schedule, rather than any fear of being judged or criticized by others. While I definitely beat myself up internally for not coping well, the main driver is just feeling like everything is too much to face.\n\nDoctor: Can you describe if there are any times when you feel overwhelmed but are still able to push through and participate in activities, or does feeling overwhelmed always lead to avoidance and shutting down for you?\n\nPatient: Lately, feeling overwhelmed almost always leads to me shutting down and avoiding things instead of pushing through. I end up just staying in my apartment, scrolling on my phone, and skipping my classes, work shifts, or favorite maker meetups. It all just feels like way too much to handle, so I can't seem to force myself to participate.\n\nDoctor: Can you tell me if you've experienced any significant stressors or traumatic events recently, such as a major life change or loss, that might be contributing to your feelings of overwhelm and avoidance?\n\nPatient: Yes, I had a bunch of huge life changes hit me all at once about a month ago. I started my first full-time factory job, began a demanding industrial maintenance program at the community college, and moved out of my parents' house in Fayette into my own apartment. Trying to balance the shift work, rent, and heavy classes all of a sudden has just completely piled up on me and feels like too much.\n\nDoctor: Can you tell me if you've ever had a period in your life where you didn't feel overwhelmed and were able to manage your responsibilities and activities without shutting down, and if so, what was different about that time compared to now?\n\nPatient: Before all this, like back in high school, I managed my time fine and was busy but excited, still having plenty of time for hobbies like basketball, theater set design, hiking, and painting. But now, the sudden combination of living on my own, paying bills, working full-time shifts, and taking demanding evening classes has completely overwhelmed me and caused me to shut down.\n\nDoctor: Can you clarify if your avoidance of activities is primarily driven by a desire to escape from the emotional distress of feeling overwhelmed, or is it more about avoiding the tasks themselves due to feeling unable to cope with their demands?\n\nPatient: It’s really a combination of both. The heavy pressure of my tasks and schedule makes me feel completely unable to cope, which leaves me constantly on edge. To escape that stressful feeling and the guilt of falling behind, I just shut down, stay in my apartment, and avoid everything by scrolling on my phone.\n\nDoctor: Can you tell me if there's a specific time frame or situation where your avoidance of activities and feelings of overwhelm started, or was it a gradual process that built up over time?\n\nPatient: It started pretty suddenly, within just a few weeks of starting the factory job, moving into my own apartment, and beginning the maintenance program all at once. It wasn't a slow, gradual buildup over years; this has only been going on for about a month now, ever since all those changes hit me at the same time.\n\nDoctor: You mentioned that these feelings of overwhelm and avoidance started about a month ago, after several significant life changes. I haven't really had any periods of improvement because the school and work pressure hasn't let up at all. Instead, I've just consistently found myself avoiding my responsibilities and zoning out on my phone.\n\nDoctor: When you're feeling overwhelmed and shut down, do you feel a lack of emotional response or interest in activities you normally enjoy, or is it more that you're actively trying to avoid the stress and pressure of those activities?\n\nPatient: It is definitely more about actively avoiding the stress and pressure because everything just feels like too much. I still care about my hobbies, like the maker meetup, but I feel too overwhelmed to show up. Instead, I end up staying in my apartment, scrolling on my phone, and avoiding things to escape the pressure.\n\nDoctor: Can you clarify if there are times when you feel emotionally numb or detached from activities you used to enjoy, rather than just avoiding them due to feeling overwhelmed?\n\nPatient: It’s not really about feeling emotionally numb or detached, because I still care a lot about my hobbies like painting, basketball, and the maker meetup. I just avoid them because I feel completely overwhelmed and exhausted by my schedule. When I zone out on my phone, it's more of an avoidance tactic because everything feels like too much, rather than a lack of feeling.\n\nDoctor: Can you tell me if there's a specific situation or task where you feel like you're avoiding it because you're afraid of not being able to do it perfectly, versus avoiding it solely because it feels overwhelming?\n\nPatient: It's definitely not about a fear of not doing things perfectly. I avoid going to my classes or my maker meetup solely because I feel completely on edge and have too much on my plate to handle all at once. Instead of facing it, I just sit in my apartment scrolling on my phone because everything feels like too much to face.\n\nDoctor: Do you ever feel like you've lost interest in things you used to enjoy, or is it just that you're avoiding them because they feel overwhelming?"

It's putting my spot in the tech program and my actual job at serious risk.\n\nDoctor: Can you tell me if there are any specific situations or tasks that you avoid due to feeling overwhelmed, but you're still able to force yourself to participate in or complete, or do you tend to avoid everything when you're feeling overwhelmed?\n\nPatient: When I get overwhelmed, I don't really force myself through things; I tend to just shut down and avoid almost everything. I end up skipping my evening classes, missing my favorite maker meetup, and even swapping my work shifts at the last minute just to stay in my apartment scrolling on my phone.\n\nDoctor: Do you feel like you're avoiding activities because you're worried about not being able to do them perfectly, or is it solely because you feel overwhelmed and exhausted by the thought of doing them?\n\nPatient: It’s definitely not about trying to be perfect. I just feel constantly on edge, and the sheer volume of work, school, and moving makes everything feel like \"too much.\" That's what causes me to shut down, avoid my classes and meetups, and just scroll on my phone instead.\n\nDoctor: Can you tell me if there's a point where you feel like you've completely given up on your goals and activities, or do you still hold onto the idea that you'll get back to them once you feel less overwhelmed?\n\nPatient: No, I haven't given up entirely. I really think I'll be able to handle things and get back to my normal activities once I adjust.\n\nDoctor: Can you describe if there's a specific difference in how you feel when you're avoiding activities due to feeling overwhelmed versus when you're engaging in avoidance as a way to escape from emotional distress, or do these feelings blend together for you?\n\nPatient: Honestly, those feelings pretty much blend together for me.
